title: A theoretical framework for efficient solvent suppression in solid-state NMR: Circumventing solvent-signal refocusing by adiabatic-inversion-based dephasing
excerpt: A theoretical framework explaining why the SLAP solvent-suppression scheme outperforms MISSISSIPPI in solid-state NMR: MISSISSIPPI is limited by solvent-signal refocusing, whereas SLAP circumvents echo formation by design, confirmed by simulations and 1H-detected experiments on GB1 at 60 kHz MAS.
citation: Matsunaga, T.†, Okabe, R.†, Liu, Y., Shigemitsu, Y., & Ishii, Y. (2026). A theoretical framework for efficient solvent suppression in solid-state NMR: Circumventing solvent-signal refocusing by adiabatic-inversion-based dephasing. Journal of Magnetic Resonance 392, 108183.

title: Agentic AI for Scientific Reasoning in Autonomous Quantum Sensing Experiments
excerpt: An LLM-based agentic workflow that autonomously plans, runs, and analyzes quantum sensing experiments on nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, together with offline benchmarks that evaluate the agent's scientific reasoning.
citation: Isogawa, T.†, Okabe, R.†, Phadetsuwannukun, N., Li, M., & Cappellaro, P. (2026). Agentic AI for Scientific Reasoning in Autonomous Quantum Sensing Experiments. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.25145.

title: Universal Magnetic Structure Prediction from Atomic Coordinates with Near-Experimental Accuracy
excerpt: Magnetic structure network (MSN), an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network trained on experimentally determined MAGNDATA structures, predicts collinear and non-collinear magnetic structures from atomic coordinates using a primitive modulated structure representation that unifies commensurate and incommensurate orders.
citation: Chotrattanapituk, A.†, Okabe, R.†, Rha, E., Al-Hinai, M., Jiang, E., Pajerowski, D., Cheng, Y., Turner, J.J., & Li, M. (2026). Universal Magnetic Structure Prediction from Atomic Coordinates with Near-Experimental Accuracy. arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.16230.

title: Quantum Theory of Functionally Graded Materials
excerpt: An ab initio quantum framework for the electromagnetic properties of functionally graded materials, whose aperiodic composition breaks Bloch's theorem: modulated Bloch states, effective field equations, and a generalized WKB method valid in the fully quantum regime yield position-dependent conductivity and permeability.
citation: Landry, M.J.†, Okabe, R.†, Fu, C., & Li, M. (2026). Quantum Theory of Functionally Graded Materials. arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.03424.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven approaches for materials design and discovery
excerpt: A Review of computational materials design over the past decades, from high-throughput forward machine learning and evolutionary algorithms to reinforcement learning and deep generative models, highlighting the shift from screening to inverse generation and the open challenges ahead.
citation: Cheng, M.†, Fu, C.†, Okabe, R.†, Chotrattanapituk, A.†, Boonkird, A., Hung, N.T., & Li, M. (2026). Artificial intelligence-driven approaches for materials design and discovery. Nature Materials 25, 174-190.

title: Structural Constraint Integration in a Generative Model for the Discovery of Quantum Materials
excerpt: SCIGEN enforces geometric constraints such as honeycomb and kagome lattices within diffusion-based generative models, generating ten million candidate compounds with Archimedean and Lieb lattices; over 10% pass multistage stability screening, and a GNN classifier detects magnetic ordering in 41% of DFT-relaxed structures.
citation: Okabe, R., Cheng, M., Chotrattanapituk, A., Mandal, M., Mak, K., Cordova Carrizales, D., Hung, N.T., Fu, X., Han, B., Wang, Y., Xie, W., Cava, R.J., Jaakkola, T.S., Cheng, Y., Li, M. (2025). Structural Constraint Integration in a Generative Model for the Discovery of Quantum Materials. Nature Materials 25, 223-230.

title: Are Quantum Materials Economically and Environmentally Sustainable?
excerpt: A perspective assessing the economic and environmental sustainability of quantum materials, examining element criticality, cost, and supply considerations for the materials that underpin quantum technologies.
citation: Boonkird, A.†, Cheng, M.†, Chotrattanapituk, A.†, Cordova Carrizales, D., Okabe, R., Drucker, N.C., Mandal, M., Nguyen, T., Yeo, J., Belosevich, V., Spero, E., Ortiz, C., Ma, Q., Fu, L., Palacios, T., Niroui, F., & Li, M. (2025). Are Quantum Materials Economically and Environmentally Sustainable? Materials Today 90, 241-248.

title: Tuning Chiral Anomaly Signature in a Dirac Semimetal via Fast-Ion Implantation
excerpt: Fast-ion implantation of Nb-doped Cd3As2 thin films enhances the negative longitudinal magnetoresistance signature of the chiral anomaly by more than 100% relative to pristine films while maintaining crystallinity, establishing high-energy implantation as a route to chiralitronic properties.
citation: Mandal, M.†, Rha, E.†, Chotrattanapituk, A.†, Cordova Carrizales, D.†, Lygo, A., Woller, K.B., Cheng, M., Okabe, R., Zhu, G., Kishida, S., Mak, K., Fu, C.L., Michalopoulos, S., Liu, C., Wu, L., Zhu, Y., Stemmer, S., & Li, M. (2025). Tuning Chiral Anomaly Signature in a Dirac Semimetal via Fast-Ion Implantation. Nano Letters 25, 51, 17571–17577.

title: Closing the superconducting gap with AI
excerpt: A short perspective on using AI to predict superconducting gaps, discussing how machine learning can complement first-principles approaches in the search for new superconductors.
citation: Cheng, M., Okabe, R., & Li, M. (2025). Closing the superconducting gap with AI. Newton 1, 100093.

title: AI-driven defect engineering in advanced thermoelectric materials
excerpt: A review of how AI and machine learning are transforming thermoelectric materials design, from deep and graph-based models that capture structure–property relations in a multiscale defect space to AI-enhanced defect engineering and inverse design.
citation: Fu, C.†, Cheng, M.†, Hung, N.T.†, Rha, E., Chen, Z., Okabe, R., Cordova Carrizales, D., Mandal, M., Cheng, Y.Q., & Li, M. (2025). AI-driven defect engineering in advanced thermoelectric materials. Advanced Materials 37, 2505642.

title: AI-Powered Exploration of Molecular Vibrations, Phonons and Spectroscopy
excerpt: A review of AI-driven methods for atomic vibrations: databases, structural representations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, graph neural networks, and emerging approaches that accelerate predictions of lattice dynamics, phonons, molecular dynamics, and vibrational spectra.
citation: Han, B.†, Okabe, R.†, Chotrattanapituk, A.†, Cheng, M.†, Li, M., & Cheng, Y. (2025). AI-Powered Exploration of Molecular Vibrations, Phonons and Spectroscopy. Digital Discovery.

title: Quantum Theory of X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy
excerpt: A microscopic quantum theory of X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy derived from electron–photon interaction Hamiltonians, introducing four configurations tied to distinct fourth-order density correlations and a generalized Siegert relation, which breaks down even for a non-interacting Fermi gas.
citation: Siriviboon, P.†, Fu, C.†, Landry, M.†, Okabe, R., Cordova Carrizales, D., Wang, Y., & Li, M. (2024). Quantum Theory of X-ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy. arXiv preprint arXiv:2412.03635.

title: Large Language Model-Guided Prediction Toward Quantum Materials Synthesis
excerpt: A framework that uses large language models to predict synthesis pathways for inorganic and quantum materials, turning literature-scale synthesis knowledge into actionable suggestions of precursors, reactions, and conditions.
citation: Okabe, R.†, West, Z.†, Chotrattanapituk, A., Cheng, M., Cordova Carrizales, D., Xie, W., Cava, R.J., & Li, M. (2024). Large Language Model-Guided Prediction Toward Quantum Materials Synthesis. arXiv preprint arXiv:2410.20976.

title: Universal Ensemble-Embedding Graph Neural Network for Direct Prediction of Optical Spectra from Crystal Structures
excerpt: GNNOpt, an equivariant graph neural network with universal ensemble embedding, predicts optical spectra such as refractive index and absorption directly from crystal structures, enabling high-throughput screening of materials for light–matter applications.
citation: Hung, N.T., Okabe, R., Chotrattanapituk, A., & Li, M. (2024). Ensemble-Embedding Graph Neural Network for Direct Prediction of Optical Spectra from Crystal Structure. Advanced Materials, 2409175.

title: Virtual Node Graph Neural Network for Full Phonon Prediction
excerpt: Virtual node graph neural networks predict Γ-phonon spectra and full phonon dispersions directly from atomic coordinates, orders of magnitude faster than machine-learning interatomic potentials with comparable accuracy, enabling a Γ-phonon database of over 146,000 materials.
citation: Okabe, R.†, Chotrattanapituk, A.†, Boonkird, A., Andrejevic, N., Fu, X., Jaakkola, T.S., Song, Q., Nguyen, T., Drucker, N.C., Mu, S., Liao, B., Cheng, Y., & Li, M. (2024). Virtual Node Graph Neural Network for Full Phonon Prediction. Nature Computational Science 4, 522-531.

title: Machine Learning Detection of Majorana Zero Modes from Zero Bias Peak Measurements
excerpt: A machine learning framework distinguishes Majorana zero modes from spurious zero-bias peaks using quantum transport simulations and topological data analysis, reaching 85% accuracy on 1D and 94% on 2D conductance data with Zeeman splitting.
citation: Cheng, M., Okabe, R., Chotrattanapituk, A., & Li, M. (2024). Machine Learning Detection of Majorana Zero Modes from Zero Bias Peak Measurements. Matter 7, 2507.

title: Precise Fermi-level engineering in a topological Weyl semimetal via fast ion implantation
excerpt: Accelerator-based high-energy hydrogen implantation, guided by theory-driven planning, tunes the Fermi level of the bulk Weyl semimetal TaP with meV precision around the Weyl nodes while preserving crystallinity, the Weyl nodes, and carrier mobility.
citation: Mandal, M.†, Chotrattanapituk, A.†, Woller, K., Xu, H., Mao, N., Okabe, R., Boonkird, A., Nguyen, T., Drucker, N.C., Momiki, T., Li, J., Kong, J., & Li, M. (2024). Precise Fermi-level engineering in a topological Weyl semimetal via fast ion implantation. Applied Physics Reviews 11, 021429.

title: Tetris-Inspired Detector with Neural Network for Radiation Mapping
excerpt: A radiation mapping framework using Tetris-inspired detector pixels: inter-pixel padding plus neural networks trained on Monte Carlo data let a detector with as few as four pixels predict source direction, and a moving detector with maximum a posteriori estimation localizes sources, verified in field tests.
citation: Okabe, R.†, Xue, S.†, Vavrek, J.†, Yu, J., Pavlovsky, R., Negut, V., Quiter, B., Cates, J., Liu, T., Forget, B., Jegelka, S., Kohse, G., Hu, L-W., & Li, M. (2024). Tetris-Inspired Detector with Neural Network for Radiation Mapping. Nature Communications 15, 3061.

title: Incipient Nematicity from Electron Flat Bands in a Kagome Metal
excerpt: Thermodynamic, dilatometry, resonant X-ray, inelastic neutron, Larmor diffraction, and thermoelectric measurements reveal an unconventional, incipient nematic order in the kagome metal CoSn near 225 K, explained by thermally excited flat bands that promote symmetry breaking.
citation: Drucker, N.C., Nguyen, T., Mandal, M., Siriviboon, P., Quan, Y., Boonkird, A., Okabe, R., Li, F., Burrage, K., Funuma, F., Matsuda, M., Abernathy, D., Williams, T., Chi, S., Ye, F., Nelson, C., Liao, B., Volkov, P., & Li, M. (2024). Incipient Nematicity from Electron Flat Bands in a Kagome Metal. arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.17141.

title: Materials Informatics for the Development and Discovery of Future Magnetic Materials
excerpt: A summary of recent developments in AI- and ML-driven searches for magnetic materials, with a flowchart to guide the choice of approach and an overview of work on topological materials, Heusler alloys, interfaces, and permanent magnets, based on the IEEE Intermag 2023 symposium.
citation: Okabe, R., Li, M., Iwasaki, Y., Regnault, N., Felser, C., Shirai, M., Kovacs, A., Schrefl, T., & Hirohata, A. (2023). Materials Informatics for the Development and Discovery of Future Magnetic Materials. IEEE Magnetic Letters 14, 1-5.

title: Topological superconductors from a materials perspective
excerpt: A materials perspective on topological superconductors: a short review of the basics and theory, an overview of natural and synthetic candidate materials, and the experimental signatures used to identify them, with a call for new signatures and stronger computational support.
citation: Mandal, M., Drucker, N.C., Siriviboon, P., Nguyen, T., Boonkird, A., Lamichhane, T.N., Okabe, R., Chotrattanapituk, A., & Li, M. (2023). Topological superconductors from a materials perspective. Chemistry of Materials 35, 16, 6184–6200.

title: Challenges and Opportunities of Machine Learning on Neutron and X-ray Scattering
excerpt: A feature article surveying how machine learning is reshaping neutron and X-ray scattering, from phase mapping and crystallographic analysis to super-resolution small-angle scattering, and the criteria that determine when ML-based analysis succeeds.
citation: Drucker, N.C., Liu, T., Chen, Z., Okabe, R., Chotrattanapituk, A., Nguyen, T., Wang, Y., & Li, M. (2022). Challenges and Opportunities of Machine Learning on Neutron and X-ray Scattering. Synchrotron Radiation News 35, 16-20.

title: Machine Learning Magnetism Classifiers from Atomic Coordinates
excerpt: A Euclidean-equivariant graph neural network classifies magnetic order directly from atomic coordinates, using a descriptor that encodes crystal structures of any space group, as a data-driven complement to neutron diffraction and semi-empirical DFT.
citation: Merker, H.A., Heiberger, H., Nguyen, L., Liu, T., Chen, Z., Andrejevic, N., Drucker, N.C., Okabe, R., Wang, Y., Smidt, T., & Li, M. (2022). Machine Learning Magnetism Classifiers from Atomic Coordinates. iScience 25, 10, 105192.

title: Efficient solvent suppression with adiabatic inversion for 1H-detected solid-state NMR
excerpt: SLAP, a solvent-suppression scheme based on adiabatic inversion pulses for 1H-detected solid-state NMR, achieves up to 3.5-fold better suppression than MISSISSIPPI on a uniformly 13C/15N-labeled GB1 sample at 60 kHz magic-angle spinning, at lower average RF power.
citation: Matsunaga, T., Okabe, R., & Ishii, Y. (2021). Efficient solvent suppression with adiabatic inversion for 1H-detected solid-state NMR. Journal of Biomolecular NMR 12, 365-370.

title: A Conductive Metal-Organic Framework Photoanode
excerpt: Photosensitizing arrays built from conductive metal–organic frameworks enable light harvesting and efficient charge separation, demonstrated as a conductive MOF photoanode.
citation: Pattengale, B., Freeze, J.G., Guberman-Pfeffer, M., Okabe, R., Ostresh, S., Chaudhuri, S., Batista, V.S., & Schmuttenmaer, C.A. (2020). A Conductive Metal-Organic Framework Photoanode. Chemical Science 11, 9593–9603.

title: Metal-Organic Framework Photoconductivity via Time-Resolved Terahertz Spectroscopy
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
excerpt: Time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy, combined with a new sample preparation method, measures the photoconductivity of the conductive MOF Zn2TTFTB without contacts, resolving sub-picosecond carrier dynamics with two distinct lifetimes and Drude–Smith frequency dependence.
citation: Pattengale, B., Neu, J., Ostresh, S., Hu, G., Spies, J.A., Okabe, R., Brudvig, G.W., & Schmuttenmaer, C.A. (2019). Metal-Organic Framework Photoconductivity via Time-Resolved Terahertz Spectroscopy. Journal of the American Chemical Society 141, 9793–9797.
